## Why it matters internationally

BAM's Division 8.3 Thermographic Methods develops contactless thermographic testing,
with in-situ monitoring of additive manufacturing as a named work area. It runs
SAMMIE, an open-architecture laser powder bed fusion testbed instrumented with
thermographic and optical sensors, on which it has demonstrated hyperspectral SWIR
measurement of absolute melt-pool temperatures. Its published work treats the
unknown, changing emissivity of metal surfaces as the key obstacle to quantitative
in-situ thermography, and addresses it with spectral directional emissivity
measurements (carried out with CAE Würzburg) and multispectral methods.

## Scope of activity

- **Quantities:** absolute melt-pool temperature fields in laser powder bed fusion (hyperspectral SWIR thermography) · spectral directional emissivity of PBF-LB/M surfaces and powders (316L, AlSi10Mg), measured with CAE Würzburg · multispectral optical tomography signals
- **Spectral range:** 0.9–1.7 µm (SWIR hyperspectral line imaging)
- **Temperature:** Melt-pool temperatures of about 1300–2700 K observed in situ (Breese & Altenburg 2025)
- **Methodology:** Hyperspectral SWIR measurement of spectral exitance along a line, converted to absolute temperature with Planck's law and a spectral emissivity function, on an open-architecture laser powder bed fusion testbed under argon; complemented by multispectral optical tomography and active laser thermography.
- **Named facilities:** SAMMIE — Sensor-based Additive Manufacturing Machine (PBF-LB/M testbed)

**Application domains:** in-situ monitoring and quality assurance in laser powder bed fusion of metals · in-situ defect detection by active laser thermography · thermographic non-destructive testing.
